R6.5.response:
You are right, and we have rebuilt the comparison rather than defended it. Comparing a detector trained on 2.5 million imbalanced flows against baselines trained on a 10,000-flow class-balanced subset is not a comparison, and presenting the two in adjacent tables invited exactly the reading you describe.

Every method is now run twice by us, on the same machine, on the CPU, under one measurement harness. Protocol A is the full chronological split at the natural class prevalence: 2,513,556 training and 1,077,238 test flows, no subsampling, no artificial balancing. Protocol B applies the same subsampling to every classical baseline, 100,000 training and 40,000 test flows preserving the natural class ratio rather than balancing it, with the one exception stated below; the deep-learning rows of Table 20 carry their own departures, each recorded in that table's caption. Both protocols are defined in Sec. VI-B rather than in the tables that use them. The two are reported in separate tables and never mixed, and the headline comparison is Protocol A, because that is the setting the detector is claimed to operate in.

The result is less flattering than the submitted version and more informative. Under Protocol A the detector reaches 97.88 percent macro F1, statistically indistinguishable from LightGBM at 97.89 percent, and it no longer has a unique claim to the top of any accuracy column. What it does have is the lowest false positive rate of any method tested, by a factor of four: 0.095 percent against 0.371 percent for LightGBM, which over the test partition is 29 false alarms against 113. It is also the slowest tree model per flow, at 7.05 milliseconds against 0.26 for LightGBM, and we treat that as the configuration defect it is rather than omitting it.

Two baselines could not be run at full scale and we state the cap rather than dropping them. The RBF kernel SVM is quadratic in the sample count and appears only under Protocol B, where it is fitted on 40,000 of the 100,000 training flows for the same quadratic reason, making it the one classical baseline in Protocol B not fitted on the full Protocol B training block. Because a figure measured on 40,000 flows does not belong in a column measured on 1,077,238, we report it in the text of Sec. VIII-A rather than in either table, and we say there that it is not like-for-like. The linear SVM had not converged after thirty minutes on the full partition, so it is fitted on a capped subsample of 300,000 flows, which is marked in Table 19 and stated in the text. We would rather report a capped baseline with the cap visible than report only the baselines that happened to be convenient.
R6.5.action: Replaced the class-balanced subset comparison with two protocols applied identically to every model, reported them in separate tables with a statement that they answer different questions, added the false-positive column that the comparison turns on, and stated every training cap explicitly.
R6.5.location: Sec. VIII-A (Baseline comparison) and Table 19, Sec. VI-B (Evaluation protocol), Sec. VI-C (Computing environment)
